title: Amazing Animal Bodies!
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Milo the bluebird, and welcome to The Animated Zoo!
Today we're looking at amazing animal bodies. Necks, ears, tails, paws and legs!
Can you count five animals with me? One, two, three, four, five!

lines: Here's our first animal. Here's a clue: it has a super long neck! Can you guess?
Let's fly up high to the giraffes!
Giraffes are the tallest animals in the world.
Their long necks help them reach leaves at the tops of trees.
Can you stretch up tall like a giraffe? Stretch, stretch!
Can you guess how many bones are in a giraffe's long neck?
Seven! That's the same number of neck bones as you have!
A giraffe's neck bones are just much, much bigger.
A baby giraffe is called a calf.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has big floppy ears and a long trunk! Can you guess?
Let's stomp over to the elephants!
Elephants are the biggest animals on land.
An elephant uses its trunk to smell, to drink, and to pick things up.
Can you flap your arms like big elephant ears? Flap, flap!
Can you guess why elephants flap their ears?
To cool down! Flapping their big ears helps them stay cool on hot days.
Their ears work a bit like a fan.
African elephants have the biggest ears of all.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it hops, and it carries its baby in a pouch! Can you guess?
Let's hop over to the kangaroos!
Kangaroos have big, strong back legs for hopping.
Can you hop like a kangaroo? Hop, hop, hop!
Can you guess what a kangaroo uses like an extra leg?
Its tail! When a kangaroo walks slowly, its strong tail works like a fifth leg.
One, two, three, four, five legs! What a clever tail.
A kangaroo family group is called a mob.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has white fur, and it lives where it's icy and snowy! Can you guess?
Let's fly north to the polar bears! Brrr!
Polar bears live in the cold, snowy Arctic.
They are big, strong swimmers, too.
Can you tiptoe like you're walking on ice? Careful, careful!
Can you guess how polar bears walk on slippery snow?
Their paws have tiny bumps, like the bottom of a sneaker! The bumps help them grip.
Let's say it together: POLAR BEAR!
Fur on their paws helps keep their feet warm, too.
Our last animal! Here's a clue: it's pink, and it has long skinny legs! Can you guess?
Let's tiptoe to the pond to see the flamingos!
Flamingos eat with their heads upside down!
They like to live together in big groups.
Can you stand on one leg like a flamingo? Wobble, wobble!
Can you guess why flamingos stand on one leg?
Scientists think it helps them rest, and save their energy!
A flamingo can even sleep standing on one leg.

recap: What an amazing adventure! Let's remember.
Giraffes have seven neck bones, just like you.
Elephants flap their ears to cool down.
Kangaroos use their tails like a fifth leg.
Polar bears have bumpy paws to grip the snow.
And flamingos rest standing on one leg!
outro: Which animal was your favorite? Remember, be kind to every animal. Watch quietly and give them space.
Bye, friends! See you at the zoo!
